newsitem.title: CUBA: Most Cuban churches with the revolution - official.
newsitem.headline: Most Cuban churches with the revolution - official.

text.p: A Cuban Communist Party official said on Monday the party favoured respect for all religious institutions and believers and added that, in turn, most of the island's churches "accompany" the revolution.

Caridad Diego, head of the party's religious affairs department, was quoted by the Cuban news agency Prensa Latina as saying there had been a positive evolution in the relations between authorities and the island's churches.

"The vast majority of churches existing in the country accompany the current revolutionary process, and an important part of the faithful are active with this process," Diego told a parliamentary committee on foreign relations.
Diego did not single out any particular church as being less favourable toward the system.
Despite moves toward more religious tolerance in Cuba since the late 1980s, tensions persisted with the country's Roman Catholic Church, although these have eased notably in recent months.
Last month President Fidel Castro met Pope John Paul at the Vatican and it was agreed the pontiff would visit Cuba next year.
In past years, Catholic bishops have irritated authorities with criticism of the political system.

Diego did not mention the Catholic Church. But she said that "each day the use of the pulpit to put people against the revolution is less, and when this does happen we discuss it with church authorities."
She added that an important number of believers rejected what she called subversion of the system using the churches.

Diego was speaking just ahead of Christmas, which is not recognised as a holiday in Cuba. Parliament, which meets for only several days a year, is holding its sole two-day session of the year on Dec. 24 and 25.

The timing has surprised some foreign observers, who had thought authorities might make a gesture to recognise the major Christian festival amid their current eforts to improve relations with the Catholic Church.
The Christmas holiday was cancelled in Cuba, officially a lay state, in 1969 and has not been restored.
